# Violin plots {#sec-violin-plots}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()

ggplot2::theme_set(ggrewindr::theme_microdrive(

```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_microdrive()`

Graphs in this chapter use `ggrewindr::theme_microdrive()`, built from IBM and Hitachi Microdrive cards on a tan desk: a black frame, a red title, IBM blue, red, navy, and Hitachi sky blue marks, and a Times New Roman title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1999)
microdrive_photos <- tibble(
  photo_id = 1:300,
  size_mb = round(rlnorm(n = 300, meanlog = log(0.75), sdlog = 0.8), 2)
)
labs_violin <- labs(
  title = "IBM Microdrive photo file sizes",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "300 photos saved to a 340MB card in 1999",
  x = "",
  y = "File size (MB)")
ggp2_violin <- ggplot(data = microdrive_photos,
       aes(x = '', 
           y = size_mb)) +
       geom_violin() 
ggp2_violin + 
  labs_violin
```

::::

## Description

Violin plots show data distribution and probability density. They are like box plots (@sec-box-plots) but have a rotated kernel density plot on each side. We can use them to compare distributions across categories.

::: {.column-margin}

The violin plot is a mirrored density plot. It draws a smoothed distribution on both sides of a center line, which creates a Rorschach-like inkblot:

![source: Rorschach test, Wikipedia](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/70/Rorschach_blot_01.jpg){fig-align="right" width="80%"}
:::

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}
Install packages.
:::


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}
In 1999, IBM's 340MB Microdrive squeezed a tiny spinning hard disk into a CompactFlash Type II card, giving digital camera owners room for hundreds of photos. The photo files varied a lot in size. Most JPEGs came in under a megabyte, but detailed scenes and high quality settings produced a few much larger files. We'll simulate 300 photo files with `rlnorm()`, rounding each size to the nearest hundredth of a megabyte. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 300 file sizes every time you run the code below.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1999) # same 300 photos every time the code runs
microdrive_photos <- tibble(
  photo_id = 1:300, # 300 different photos, one row each
  size_mb = round(
    rlnorm(n = 300, meanlog = log(0.75), sdlog = 0.8), # file sizes (most near 0.75 MB, a few much larger)
    2 # two decimal places
    )
)
glimpse(microdrive_photos)
```
:::

## Distribution

File sizes are a classic example of data that can't go below zero but can stretch a long way above it. That gives the violin a wide base and a long, thin neck. The trick to understanding this shape is the logarithm: on a log scale, these file sizes turn into the familiar bell curve from @sec-histograms. Below we'll move from the file sizes, to a picture, to the formula. Then we'll change the data to see what the violin shows when the photos stop following the formula.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first ten photos.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(microdrive_photos$size_mb, 10)
```
:::

Most of these are under 1.5 MB, but three are near or above 2 MB. A few large files like these pull the mean well above the median. Taking the log of each file size shrinks the gap.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
microdrive_photos |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(size_mb), 
    median = median(size_mb),
    mean_log = mean(log(size_mb)),
    median_log = median(log(size_mb)))
```
:::

On the megabyte scale, the mean is about `r round(mean(microdrive_photos$size_mb) - median(microdrive_photos$size_mb), 2)` MB higher than the median. On the log scale, the mean and median are almost identical, which is what we'd expect from a symmetric distribution.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

A bar model splits the photos at 0.75 MB (we'll see why in a moment). The two parts are close to equal, so 0.75 MB sits near the middle of the file sizes.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_bar_model_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.45
microdrive_photos |> 
  mutate(range = factor(if_else(size_mb < 0.75, "under 0.75 MB", "0.75 MB or more"),
    levels = c("under 0.75 MB", "0.75 MB or more"))) |> 
  count(range) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = "300 photos", fill = range)) + 
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = n), color = "white", 
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE)) + 
  labs(x = "Number of photos", y = NULL, fill = "File size")
```
:::

Below are two violins of the same 300 file sizes. The first uses megabytes, so most of the area is squashed near the bottom and the neck stretches up past 5 MB. The second puts the `y` axis on a log scale with `scale_y_log10()`, which turns the same file sizes into a symmetric shape centered near 0.75 MB.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(data = microdrive_photos, aes(x = "", y = size_mb)) + 
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") + 
  labs(title = "Megabyte scale", x = NULL, y = "File size (MB)")

ggplot(data = microdrive_photos, aes(x = "", y = size_mb)) + 
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(title = "Log scale", x = NULL, y = "File size (MB, log scale)")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

The `rlnorm()` call that created the data draws from a [log normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log-normal_distribution). A file size is log normal when its logarithm is normal:

$$
\log(X) \sim \text{Normal}(\mu = \log(0.75), \sigma = 0.8)
$$

The two parameters describe the log scale, not the megabyte scale. Back on the megabyte scale, the median is $e^{\mu} = 0.75$ MB, which is why the bar model split the photos at 0.75 MB. The mean is larger, $e^{\mu + \sigma^2 / 2} = 0.75 \times e^{0.32} \approx 1.03$ MB, because the long right tail pulls it up. The bigger $\sigma$ gets, the longer the violin's neck and the further the mean drifts from the median.

Our simulated photos come close: the median is `r round(median(microdrive_photos$size_mb), 2)` MB and the mean is `r round(mean(microdrive_photos$size_mb), 2)` MB.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CHANGE IT:**
:::

So far the file sizes look the way the formula says they should. Now suppose the photographer switches the camera to uncompressed TIFF for the last 50 photos. TIFFs fill a card fast, so she swaps in a second Microdrive. Each TIFF lands near 3.6 MB, and we'd expect them to add a second bump high on the violin's neck.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: change_data_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1999)
tiff_photos <- microdrive_photos
tiff_photos$size_mb[251:300] <- round(
  rnorm(n = 50, mean = 3.6, sd = 0.2), # uncompressed TIFF files near 3.6 MB
  2)
tiff_photos |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(size_mb), 
    median = median(size_mb),
    q3 = quantile(size_mb, 0.75))
```
:::

Below are the same two violins, drawn with the TIFF photos.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: change_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(data = tiff_photos, aes(x = "", y = size_mb)) + 
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") + 
  labs(title = "Megabyte scale", x = NULL, y = "File size (MB)")

ggplot(data = tiff_photos, aes(x = "", y = size_mb)) + 
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(title = "Log scale", x = NULL, y = "File size (MB, log scale)")
```
:::

The TIFF files give the violin a second bulge between about 3.2 and 4.1 MB. Even the log scale can't make this shape symmetric. The summary numbers barely hint at this. The median moves from 0.81 to 0.97 MB, and the mean moves from 1.07 to 1.51 MB. A box plot of the same data would only show a taller box, because the third quartile jumps from 1.35 to 2.30 MB.

I've found this is where violins earn their place. When data come from two different processes, the violin draws both shapes, while the summary numbers blend them into one.


## Grammar 

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}

Create labels with `labs()`

Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

Map an empty string (`""`) to the `x` and `size_mb` to the `y` (every photo shares one `x` value, so all 300 sizes make one unlabeled violin)

Add `geom_violin()`

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true 
#| warning: false
#| message: false
labs_violin <- labs(
  title = "IBM Microdrive photo file sizes",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "300 photos saved to a 340MB card in 1999",
  x = "",
  y = "File size (MB)")
ggp2_violin <- ggplot(data = microdrive_photos,
       aes(x = '', 
           y = size_mb)) +
       geom_violin() 
ggp2_violin + 
  labs_violin
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_violin
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_violin <- labs(
  title = "IBM Microdrive photo file sizes",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "300 photos saved to a 340MB card in 1999",
  x = "",
  y = "File size (MB)")
ggp2_violin <- ggplot(data = microdrive_photos,
       aes(x = '', 
           y = size_mb)) +
       geom_violin() 
ggp2_violin + 
  labs_violin
```
